newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks shake off losses to close higher.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks shake off losses to close higher.

text.p: Calm was restored to the Hong Kong stock market on Friday following Thursday's dramatic surge and shares overcame profit-taking pressures to finish higher.
The Hang Seng Index rose 33.52 points, or 0.25 percent, to 13,444.85 after falling to an early low of 13,336.01.

The index rose 2.33 percent on Thursday after the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping cleared uncertainties in the market. The gains prompted some to take profits while others were still looking to get into the market at lower levels.
"We yo-yoed for quite a while but the buyers won in the end," said Rory McAllister at HSBC James Capel Asia.
Turnover was HK$8.21 billion compared with HK$11.37 billion on Thursday.
Henry Lui, research analyst at Mansion House Research, said profit-taking pressures and weakness on Wall Street overnight had led to some early weakness in the market.
The Dow industrials fell 1.32 percent to 6,927.38.
But Lui said the Hong Kong market could now refocus on fundamentals after spending recent sessions glued to developments in Beijing.
"People are more confident about market sentiment after the death of Mr Deng," he said.

"They seem to think that the political situation in China will be very stable and that is why people then look back to the fundamentals of local blue chips. People will find that the earnings quality is very strong and earnings growth in the next two years will be very good."
Lui said European buyers seemed to have stepped in during the afternoon.
Analysts said the Hang Seng Index could remain around current levels next week after adding 331.59 points, or 2.53 percent, this week.

Among the major blue chips, HSBC Holdings rose HK$0.50 to HK$189.00. The banking giant is due to report its 1996 results on March 3, which should turn some of the focus next week onto banking stocks, some analysts said.
Property stocks were mixed. Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$0.50 to HK$90.50 but Henderson Land rose HK$1.00 to HK$71.50.
February Hang Seng Index futures, which expire next week, fell 60 points to 13,425.
